scenario: Two teams consume one monthly pool while a seat is removed mid-cycle and a new seat is added; a rolling horizon crosses the UTC reset.
mechanism: Per-team allowance multiplication, immediate subtraction on removal, or a fresh allowance for forecast remainder underestimates overage.
detection: Validate billing-entity pool id, effective-dated seat events, reset clock, start balance and consumption coverage.
response: Evaluate joint pool state before team allocation; preserve provider-specific asymmetric seat rules and distinguish blocked continuation from unlimited demand.
test_assertion: Proposed fixture: allowance 10, team usage 8+8, rate 1 gives overage 6, never 0; a synthetic removal with next-cycle effect does not reduce this-cycle pool; reset grants next-cycle allowance once.
residual_limit: Unknown private entitlements or missing users leave pooled-cost coverage incomplete.

scenario: Annual upfront commitment is purchased by a central account; one team becomes idle and the commitment is consumed across accounts/months.
mechanism: Adding purchase cost and covered-use valuation double-counts; forcing each month effective=billed invents adjustments; attributing only used cost drops idle commitment.
detection: Link covering/covered ids, full commitment period, payment schedule and underutilization category; assess scope completeness.
response: Maintain billed and effective views with explicit unused/central cost and complete-period bridge; do not interpret lower allocation as cancelled cash obligation.
test_assertion: Proposed $1,200 annual fixture: purchase cash is $1,200 once; policy-scheduled $100 monthly recognition sums to $1,200 over 12 months including unused cost; no requirement equates first-month billed $1,200 with effective $100.
residual_limit: Recognition schedule is fixture/finance policy, not a general accounting rule; private terms can differ.

scenario: May usage arrives in June, followed by a July correction and a cash refund in August.
mechanism: Import-date grouping labels four events as new demand; refund is deducted once from July usage and again when cash settles.
detection: Track service period, observed time, invoice period, correction reference and settlement event independently.
response: Produce separate incurred, billed and cash views; preserve signed corrections and forecast vintage instead of overwriting historical as-of truth.
test_assertion: Proposed fixture: $100 May use billed June, -$20 attributable correction in July, $20 cash refund August yields latest May net cost $80; it creates no July/August negative token demand and August refund is not a second cost correction.
residual_limit: Attribution of a general goodwill credit to a past service period may be unavailable or policy-dependent.
requirement_source: Backend actual/estimated/period provenance and transcript actuals variance concern; 02-S09, 02-S10

scenario: Usage uncertainty straddles a whole-volume pricing threshold or included-usage cliff.
mechanism: Pricing mean demand biases expected cost; assuming a monotonic cost transform mislabels quantiles; small usage increments can reprice prior consumption.
detection: Contract declares graduated versus volume mode and repricing scope; fixture evaluates each side of every boundary.
response: Price full joint demand paths; summarize charges after conversion; retain contract-specific negative incremental deltas when valid.
test_assertion: Proposed fixture F=100, allowance=10, overage rate=10 and equal-probability usage 0/20 gives mean charge 150, not g(mean usage)=100; synthetic volume rates 10 for <=100 units and 8 for >100 give costs 1000 and 808 at 100/101 units.
residual_limit: Demand distribution and correlation remain estimated; fixture checks mathematics, not enterprise calibration.
requirement_source: Master plan token counts are not dollar cost; 02-S11

scenario: A promotional grant expires near invoice period end while two eligible invoices finalize in different orders, alongside noneligible setup fees.
mechanism: A global credit subtraction assumes all charges eligible and order irrelevant; using usage date instead of contractual eligibility clock spends expired credit.
detection: Validate currency, eligible price scope, eligibility clock, expiry, remaining balance and finalization state.
response: Use actual application when reported; otherwise simulate documented order or present conditional outcomes; separate purchased face value from acquisition cost.
test_assertion: Proposed fixture: one $50 credit and two $40 eligible invoices cannot each consume $40; total applied <=50, residual eligible payable=30; excluded setup fee remains payable; expired grant applies zero when contractual invoice-end test fails.
residual_limit: Finalization order may be unknown; Stripe examples are not universal provider policy.
requirement_source: Master plan §2 vendor credits versus internal planning credits; 02-S12

scenario: Usage is priced in USD, billed in EUR with an applied source rate, settled in GBP, and invoice-only tax has recoverability unknown to the system.
mechanism: Double conversion, addition of unlike currencies, tax counted at both usage and invoice levels, or reporting FX substituted for settlement FX produces false budget headroom.
detection: Require unit/currency role, rate direction/date/source, invoice lineage and tax-inclusion policy.
response: Preserve native amounts; compute separate reporting conversion; bridge invoice tax once; leave recoverability to configured finance policy.
test_assertion: Proposed fixture USD100 at 0.9 EUR/USD yields EUR90, not EUR81; EUR9 invoice-only tax makes EUR99 gross; GBP settlement is independently linked and never summed with EUR99.
residual_limit: Future FX and tax eligibility may require conditional scenarios; no tax determination is supplied.
requirement_source: Backend units, scope and known totals; 02-S04, 02-S09

scenario: Connector delivers a revised snapshot containing a refund while another provider appends a reversal and replacement; a retry repeats a delivery.
mechanism: Appending snapshots doubles spend; replacing ledger history loses reversals; global sign filters discard refunds; retry deduplication can erase a legitimate identical adjustment.
detection: Per-source delivery scope, artifact revision/id, correction style and source-record identity.
response: Normalize snapshot replacement, delta accumulation and ledger replay separately; preserve raw artifacts and as-of versions.
test_assertion: Proposed equivalent revisions: snapshot 100 then 80; delta 100 then -20; ledger 100 then -100 then 80 each yield 80 once. Replaying the same artifact leaves 80. A distinct second -20 adjustment yields 60 when intended.
residual_limit: Identical content without stable artifact/record identifiers can remain ambiguous.
requirement_source: Backend idempotent import and reproducible actuals; 02-S05

scenario: Fixed company spend is unchanged but a team moves or another team stops usage, changing allocation weights; all usage weights later become zero.
mechanism: Allocation changes are interpreted as demand growth or savings; division by zero removes fixed obligations; stale allocation is compared with revised budgets.
detection: Version allocation policy and membership separately from provider totals; compare parent-cost and weight changes.
response: Preserve original and explicitly restated views; explain allocation-only variance; use central/default owner for zero-denominator cases; compare budgets on matched policy.
test_assertion: Proposed parent cost 100 with weights 50/50 yields 50/50; change to 80/20 yields 80/20 without company savings or new spend; zero weights assign 100 centrally under fixture policy. Each version conserves exactly 100.
residual_limit: Fair allocation is an organizational policy choice; conservation does not prove economic causality.
requirement_source: Master plan team mapping and internal budget scope; 02-S13

scenario: A tiny invoice omits a $0.50 charge from imported usage while the FOCUS rounding-tolerance floor is $1.
mechanism: Standard conformance pass is incorrectly called exact reconciliation; material relative error disappears under an absolute floor.
detection: Compute exact residual, completeness and line match separately from standard tolerance flag.
response: Show residual and category; require known rounding lineage or unresolved state; never create an unexplained balancing entry.
test_assertion: Proposed invoice 2.00 and imported charge sum 1.50 produce residual 0.50 and standard-tolerance pass, but exact-match=false and missing-line investigation remains open. Internal allocation must conserve 1.50, not silently force 2.00.
residual_limit: A smaller residual alone cannot distinguish rounding from missing data; organization chooses materiality.
owner: Invoice reconciliation and UI status contract
requirement_source: Backend known totals and visible incompleteness; transcript penny/actuals concern; 02-S06
